sections.h2: What is a lady bird deed in Florida?
sections.html:
A lady bird deed is a deed that gives an owner a life estate with enhanced powers and names who receives the property afterward. It is also called an enhanced life estate deed, and the state revenue agency has written about its tax treatment in an advisement dated October 16, 2020.

Look first at the wording of the deed itself: which powers the owner keeps and who the named remainder people are. Two deeds that both get called lady bird deeds can read differently, so the recorded text controls. Read it line by line before you plan a sale.

sections.h2: Does a lady bird deed owe Florida documentary stamp tax?
sections.html:
In the state revenue agency's advisement TAA 20B4-004, the answer was no, on the facts presented. The department concluded the deed did not transfer any present beneficial interest and was not subject to documentary stamp tax regardless of any consideration.

Those facts mattered. The life tenants in that request kept full powers over the property. A deed that gives up some of those powers could be analyzed differently, and the advisement answered one taxpayer's set of facts. Ask the county clerk of court or a Florida real estate attorney before you record, since the clerk collects the tax at recording.

For contrast, the agency's general page puts life estate deeds on its taxable list. Only the advisement's reasoning, that no present beneficial interest moves, explains why an enhanced life estate deed can be treated differently from an ordinary one.

sections.h2: How does a lady bird deed affect selling the home?
sections.html:
A sale starts with a deed to the buyer signed with the formalities Florida requires, so the first question is who must sign.

Section 689.01 requires a conveyance of an interest in land to be in writing and signed in the presence of two subscribing witnesses. A seal is not needed, and witnessing may be done by audio-video technology. Whether the named remainder people must also sign turns on the powers written into your deed. The title agent will read the recorded text before agreeing to insure, so put that question to the agent before you list.

  • Pull the recorded deed from the clerk's official records.
  • Check which powers the deed reserves to the owner, including selling and mortgaging.
  • Find out whether the underwriter will insure with only the owner signing.
  • Plan for the sale deed to be taxed at the standard doc stamp rate.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and homestead react to the deed?
sections.html:
The tax effect depends on whether a transfer counts as a change of ownership. Under section 193.155, a sale, foreclosure or other transfer of legal or beneficial title sends the assessment back to just value at the next January 1. Spousal transfers and certain transfers at death are among the exceptions.

Each year the cap is whichever is lower, 3 percent or the CPI change. Its chart shows a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024, when CPI was 3.4 percent. The advisement reasoned that no present beneficial interest passes. Whether the property appraiser's office reads your deed the same way is a separate question, and one to ask before you rely on the idea.

The homestead exemption runs up to $50,000, with the first $25,000 reaching school taxes and the second $25,000 hitting only non-school taxes on value above $50,000. Form DR-501 starts it. Renting the unit or moving out ends it.

sections.h2: Can the owner carry the tax cap to a replacement home?
sections.html:
Portability lets an owner move part of the Save Our Homes savings to a new Florida home. The new homestead must be set up within three years counted from January 1 of the year the old one was abandoned, with the sale date playing no part in that count.

Form DR-501T goes in with the new DR-501 ahead of the March 1 filing date. Section 193.155(8) reduces the new home's assessed value by the lesser of $500,000 or the gap between just value and assessed value on the old home. The statute page notes that amendments from chapter 2026-239 first apply to the 2027 tax roll, so ask the property appraiser which version applies to your filing year.

  • The old home's sale resets the buyer's assessment to just value.
  • Apply for homestead by March 1 of the tax year with the county property appraiser.
  • The home must be the permanent residence by the January 1 assessment date.
  • Homestead is lost if the unit is rented, stops being the permanent home, or the owner is no longer a Florida permanent resident.

sections.h2: How do common deed types compare for tax?
sections.html:
Deed type drives the tax result, who must sign and what the title insurer will accept, and each difference shows up at closing.

Deed typeDoc stamp tax per the Department of RevenueSource
Lady bird (enhanced life estate), on the facts in TAA 20B4-004Not subject, regardless of considerationTAA 20B4-004
Life estate deedListed as a taxable deedDOR doc stamp page
Quit claim deedListed as a taxable deedDOR doc stamp page
Personal representative's deed under a probated willListed as not taxableDOR doc stamp page

Source: Florida Department of Revenue.

Recording costs follow section 28.24, which also adds a $1.00 charge for each name beyond four on an instrument.

sections.h2: What if the owner wants to sell fast with a lady bird deed in place?
sections.html:
Cash buyers still want clean title. Gather the recorded deed, the legal description and any mortgage payoff before you talk to them.

The closing agent will verify each signer, pay off liens from proceeds and send the sale deed for recording with its tax. After an owner's death, the deed's own terms and any probate steps decide who signs next, and the underwriter will say which court papers it wants. Recording questions go to the clerk's office.

faqs.q: Is a lady bird deed subject to Florida doc stamp tax?
faqs.a: Not on the facts in state revenue advisement TAA 20B4-004, dated October 16, 2020, where the life tenants kept full powers. The department said no present beneficial interest passed, so no tax applied regardless of consideration. Confirm your own facts with the clerk or an attorney.

faqs.q: Do I need two witnesses on a lady bird deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 689.01 requires a conveyance of an interest in land to be in writing and signed in the presence of two subscribing witnesses. No seal is needed, and the witnessing may be by audio-video technology.

faqs.q: May a life tenant list and sell the property?
faqs.a: Often yes, depending on the powers your deed reserves. Show the title company the recorded deed first. It will tell you whether your signature alone is enough or whether the named remainder people must join.

faqs.q: Does a lady bird deed keep my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The exemption depends on the home staying your permanent residence, not on the deed type. Renting the home or moving out ends it, and a change of ownership resets the Save Our Homes assessment. Ask the county property appraiser how your deed is classified.

faqs.q: Which office records a lady bird deed?
faqs.a: File it at the circuit court clerk's office serving the land's county. Any documentary stamp tax is collected there at recording, along with the page fees in section 28.24.
